# ztbtrs

> Solves a triangular banded system of the form `A*X = B` or `A**H*X = B` where A is a complex triangular band matrix of order N with kd super- or sub-diagonals, and B is an N-by-NRHS matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ztbtrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztbtrs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ztbtrs( order, uplo, trans, diag, N, kd, nrhs, AB, LDAB, B, LDB ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether A is upper or lower triangular (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | Specifies the form of the system (`'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'`) |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether A is unit triangular (`'unit'` or `'non-unit'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- or sub-diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Band matrix A in band storage |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals of the triangular band matrix A. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangular band matrix A, stored in the first kd+1 rows of `AB`. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ztbtrs.ndarray(
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether A is upper or lower triangular |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | Specifies the form of the system<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'`. |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether A is unit or non-unit triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- or sub-diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right-hand side columns<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | Band matrix A in band storage |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right-hand side matrix, overwritten with solution on exit |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `diag`:

  -   `= 'N'`: A is non-unit triangular;
  -   `= 'U'`: A is unit triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals of the triangular band matrix A. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The upper or lower triangular band matrix A, stored in the first kd+1 rows of `AB`. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be 1.
- `B`: On entry, the right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the i-th diagonal element of A is zero, indicating that the matrix is singular and the solutions X have not been computed.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import ztbtrs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztbtrs';

// Upper triangular band matrix with KD=1, N=3, Dense: [3  1+i  0; 0  4  2; 0  0  5]

const AB = new Complex128Array( [ 0, 0, 3, 0, 1, 1, 4, 0, 2, 0, 5, 0 ] );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 1, 0, 2, 0, 3, 0 ] );

const info = ztbtrs( 'column-major', 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', 3, 1, 1, AB, 2, B, 3 );
console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'x (re/im pairs):', reinterpret( B, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZTBTRS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZTBTRS solves a triangular system of the form

$$
A \, X = B, A^T \, X = B, \quad\text{or}\quad A^H \, X = B
$$

where A is a triangular band matrix of order N, and B is an N-by-`NRHS` matrix. A check is made to verify that A is nonsingular.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
